requirements.requirement: worker.py continues appending the current configured message, and SIGHUP reloads a valid message.conf in the same process without creating a second writer.
requirements.summary: Before and after the node restart, journal line counts increased while running; valid replacement messages appeared after SIGHUP; the PID stayed unchanged; and exactly one matching writer existed throughout each reload test.

requirements.requirement: An empty configuration is rejected while the worker remains alive and retains the last valid message.
requirements.summary: Both bounded tests emptied message.conf and sent SIGHUP. The process remained alive with one writer and continued appending the preceding valid reload message; the original configuration was subsequently restored.
Both pre- and post-restart tests observed exit status 0, no remaining process or writer, and empty stderr after SIGTERM.
The final journal contains the original entry and exactly matches the prepared baseline SHA-256, size, ownership, permissions, and timestamp after generated test entries were removed.

requirements.requirement: The repair is installed at the requested worker.py path while preserving the installed operating-system release and kernel and using compatible software.
requirements.summary: The repaired executable is installed under /srv/legacy2/signal-driven-config-reload and passes Python 3 compilation. Before/after observations show the same RHEL 10.0 release and 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 kernel, with no package-health regression.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are directly demonstrated. The independent node-restart protocol is also complete: node1 was healthy before restart, acknowledged the scheduled restart, became temporarily unreachable, returned with a different boot ID, recovered to a healthy system state with unchanged application/data hashes, and passed the full application behavior test after restart. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.
limitations: Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The temporary legacy-worker reproduction was isolated and removed (cmd-e0cac675c3ca48a3); the worker replacement directly implemented the repair and removed its staging files (cmd-fb07ca4049b54801); the two behavior tests used bounded process, configuration, journal, and temporary-file mutations that were restored or cleaned (cmd-1dfb5599f50b4347, cmd-f080648ed8254379); the scheduled reboot served the mandatory restart protocol and its transient units disappeared with the reboot (cmd-1dc2a55969ac4f88); and the generated journal entries were removed while restoring the original journal exactly (cmd-79f6a2cdc11c4f0d). Final evidence shows no matching temporary residue, failed units, new listeners, damaged package state, or weakened security controls.
